notes: The refuter's open point (must two programs naming different padding characters get the 39 conflict?) is settled by text he did not cite. VII.4.3.4 GR8 (Implementor-Defined Element List item 86) lets the implementor choose which fixed file attributes OPEN validates. The determination is recorded at DOC-A.1-129 (2023 clause): a sequential file validates nothing beyond its organization. So GR3's fixed attribute is never compared and no 39 is required. GR2 makes padding inert on a device type it does not apply to, and every WiseOwl file is a host file whose physical record is the logical record. The probe shows no padding written, and an OPEN under a different padding character succeeds (00) and reads both records, including a record made entirely of '#'. ATTACK SURFACE: no document states that padding is 'not applicable to the device type' for every file. §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1 says 'The absence of such elements ... must be specified', and docs/CONFORMANCE.md mentions PADDING only in its obsolete-element dating.

next.reason: 1985: "Literal-1 or the value of the data item referenced by data-name-1, at the time the OPEN statement which creates the file is executed"; 2023: "No PADDING CHARACTER clause among the 2023 file control clauses; only COLLATING SEQUENCE and RECORD DELIMITER are set at OPEN". No 2023 clause holds the PADDING CHARACTER feature. The wording candidates concern other fixed file attributes, so 2023 drops the clause and this rule.
